alignments.note: Imperative rendered by the bare English verb.

Rule 20's second arm: no genitive pronoun or other source word is present to take the supplied possessive, so the article is what *your* realizes, as `τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν` → *our redemption* does; rule 11 keeps the ASV's supplied word from being mechanically `added`.
Noun stands bare, its determiner having gone to the article.

Reciprocal rendered by the two-word idiom with the dative's *to* riding along under rules 21 and 36; rule 83 heads it on *another*, the word realizing the `ἄλλος` lexeme, not on the supplied completion *one*.
SBLGNT.JAS.5.16.v016 is underdetermined and the projection's base reading is among those the English permits, so rule 12 leaves it alone; the imperative is realized by the bare verb.
Rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes `ὑπέρ`, not the verb.
Discontinuous under rule 15, the preposition standing between the two halves of the idiom; headed on *another* under rule 83.
Rule 40: the purpose conjunction is realized by the word introducing its English clause.
Rule 9: subject and auxiliaries ride with the inflected verb, headed on the lexical *healed* rather than on *ye* or *may be*.
The Greek is anarthrous, so rule 51's anarthrous clause makes the supplied *The* an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun it determines.

Substantival anarthrous adjective: rule 102's contrast scopes the supplied determiner and generic noun to helpers on the adjective where no Greek article competes, so this is rule 17's `πτωχός` → *a poor man* heading on *poor*, and the head is *righteous* rather than the supplied *man*. The genitive's *of* rides along under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Finite verb; *availeth much* is not a light-verb collapse, since `πολύ` has its own English word, so rule 2 splits the pair.
Adverbial accusative; reordered in English but recoverable as its own token.

The participle is rendered by a whole prepositional frame; *in* and *its* are supplied for it and no other source token licenses them, so they ride with it under rule 7 and rule 67's closing clause, headed on the meaning-bearing *working* under rules 17 and 91, the corpus spending *worketh*/*working* on `ἐνεργέω`. Reading *in* as `added` under rule 86 would require that no source token license it, and the participle is exactly such a token.

review_notes: Unchanged: I judge the accepted alignment correct at every unit and every head, and have only expanded three notes with the rule citations a later reader would otherwise have to reconstruct (s013, s015, s016).

Partition verified: all 16 s### ids and all 28 t### ids appear exactly once. No unit is `unrepresented`, `added` or `noncompositional`, which is right here — every source token has English and every English word has a licensing token.

The two reciprocals are the chief head decision, and rule 83 settles both: `ἀλλήλοις` → *one to another* and `ἀλλήλων` → *one … another* head on *another*, never on the supplied completion *one*, thirty corpus units to four.

s004 `τάς` → *your* follows rule 20's second arm as read by rule 76: the test is whether some other source word is available to take the supplied possessive, and this verse has none — no genitive pronoun, and `ἀλλήλοις` is already spent on the reciprocal idiom.

s015 and s014 are the same anarthrous shape decided twice: no Greek article stands in either phrase, so the supplied *The*, *a* and *man* are rule 7 helpers on the words they determine or complete, not article realizations. Rule 102 applies only where an article is present to take a determiner, and it is not.

s016 is the one place a materially different reading is available: *in its working* could be read with *in* `added` under rule 86. It is not, because rule 86's test is whether a source token licenses the supplied word, and the participle licenses the whole frame under rule 67 — which reaches for `added` only where the licensing token stands in no verse at all. The note records the competing reading.
